results.blind_working: G = F r^2/(m1 m2). Substituting dimensions: [MLT^-2][L^2]/[M^2] = [M^-1 L^3 T^-2].
F is proportional to m1 m2/r^2. Tripling one mass and doubling r gives a factor 3/2^2 = 3/4, so F' = 3F/4.
Each mass feels two forces of magnitude Gm^2/a^2 at 60° to each other. Resultant = 2F cos30° = sqrt(3) Gm^2/a^2.
Gravity cannot be shielded and is independent of the medium. A metal sheet does not reduce the force, so A is false and R is true.
Net force anywhere inside a uniform shell is zero, so I is false. By Newton's third law the apple and Earth exert equal and opposite forces on each other, so II is false.
In free fall without air resistance, every body has acceleration g whatever its mass, so the ratio is 1:1.
g' = g R^2/(R+h)^2 = g/4 gives R+h = 2R, so h = R.
At height: g(1-2h/R). At depth: g(1-d/R). Equating gives d = 2h = 32 km.
A: g/(2)^2 = g/4 (IV). B: g(1-1/2) = g/2 (II). C: g = 0 at the centre (I). D: g is proportional to rho*R, so doubling R gives 2g (III).
A true: g = GM/R^2 = (4/3)pi G rho R. B true: g = g(r/R) inside. C false: g is zero at the centre. D true: height loss 2h/R versus depth loss h/R. E false: mass is invariant.
Equal areas in equal times means constant areal velocity, dA/dt = L/(2m). The Sun's gravity is a central force, so it exerts no torque about the Sun, and L is conserved.
By Kepler's third law, T is proportional to r^(3/2). So T = 1 × 9^(3/2) = 27 years.
Angular momentum is conserved, so v_p r_p = v_a r_a. Then v_a = 6×10^4 × (2/3) = 4×10^4 m/s.
A is true because conservation of angular momentum makes speed greatest at minimum distance. R is a true statement of Kepler's third law, but it does not explain the speed variation within an orbit.
I: T^2/a^3 = 4π²/(GM_sun), independent of planet mass (neglecting tiny corrections), so incorrect. II: a = (r_min + r_max)/2, not the geometric mean (that gives the semi-minor axis), so incorrect.
V = U/m, so the unit is J/kg.
V_centre = -3GM/2R = 1.5 × V_surface = -9×10^7 J/kg.
Shell interior has V = -GM/R (IV). Solid sphere centre has V = -3GM/2R (III). U = -GMm/r (II). Field E = -dV/dr (I).
A true. B true. C false, since bound-system potential energy is negative. D true. E false, since the centre is more negative than the surface. So A, B, D.
v_e = sqrt(2GM/R) does not depend on the projectile's mass, so it stays 11.2 km/s.
With M = (4/3)πR^3ρ, v_e = R·sqrt(8πGρ/3), so v_e ∝ R at fixed density. 3 × 11.2 = 33.6 km/s.
At distance 2R from the centre, v = sqrt(2GM/2R) = 11.2/√2 = 11.2/1.414 ≈ 7.9 km/s.
Escape needs KE + PE = 0, and kinetic energy is a scalar, so the projection direction does not matter. A is false and R is true.
I: v ∝ sqrt(M/R), so R → R/4 gives v × 2, not × 4; I is incorrect. II: v ∝ R at constant density, so doubling R doubles v; II is correct.
In a circular orbit, total energy E = -KE, so E = -5×10^9 J.
By Kepler's third law, T ∝ r^{3/2}. Then T2 = 2 h × 4^{3/2} = 2 × 8 = 16 h.
KE = GMm/2r, so KE decreases as r increases. E = -GMm/2r becomes less negative, so total energy increases.
KE = GMm/2r (IV); PE = -GMm/r (I); E = -GMm/2r (III). Energy needed = -GMm/4r - (-GMm/2r) = GMm/4r (II).
A is true. B is false: gravity is not zero; the astronauts are in free fall. C is true: about 7.9 km/s and about 84 min. D is false: v = sqrt(GM/r), independent of the satellite's mass. E is true.
